client_brief:
Pulsevault: Saturday recap

Project overview
Pulsevault is an independent monthly club night in a Cleveland warehouse, run by a small crew and promoted almost entirely on social in the days after each event. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Pulsevault Saturday recap and Pulsevault cover still, graded and treated.

What we will provide
source_video_files/ (11 measured short files); motion_source_metadata.json; pulsevault_floor_stills/ (7 stills, fast lens, high ISO); pulsevault_wall_mark.jpg; pulsevault_next_date.txt; pulsevault_last_flyer.png; pulsevault_lineup_card_press.pdf; pulsevault_lineup.csv. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Pulsevault Saturday recap: A visually led highlight no longer than 15 seconds assembled only from the 11 supplied short clips, plus one platform reframe. 
- Pulsevault cover still, graded and treated: One cover from this night's floor stills, graded to a club target that keeps the stage colour rather than neutralising it, with the treatment applied as a confined move so faces stay readable at the size the cover actually posts, and a cut edge that holds...

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.

Source-media note
The supplied package contains 11 video files totaling 53.462 seconds, 0 with embedded audio, and 0 separate audio files. These measured values are the production limits.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$2,500-$6,500 fixed; target delivery 2 to 4 weeks; one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Verbatim anchor from the Freelancer.com brief quoted in the ledger's grounding_note: "I'm seeking a talented video editor to create high-energy, 30-second recaps of club nights. These videos will be used to promote future events and need to capture the vibrant atmosphere of our nights." Its stated requirements are "30-second videos", "Recaps of club nights" and an "Energetic and fast-paced vibe", with ideal skills calling out "engaging, dynamic content" for event highlight reels. The promoter and venue are laundered to the coined, IP clean night Pulsevault; no real venue, brand, artist or trademark is named. REASONABLY ENRICHED to sit inside the honest capability boundary and to be the fuller commission the same promoter actually needs: the literal post is a frame accurate Premiere and After Effects timeline edit with beat matched cuts and motion graphics, which this connector does not perform, so the recap here is produced by automatic shortening and same source reframing rather than by timeline assembly. Around it sits the rest of what a promoter posts the same night and never commissions separately: a cover still that survives being posted small, the venue's painted wall mark recovered as artwork the night can reuse, and the event details handed back as a working file, because the next date changes every month and the promoter is not going to pay a freelancer for a date change.

Around it sits the rest of what a promoter posts the same night and never commissions separately: a cover still that survives being posted small, the venue's painted wall mark recovered as artwork the night can reuse, and the event details handed back as a working file, because the next date changes every month and the promoter is not going to pay a freelancer for a date change.
price_band_and_audience: A twenty to thirty dollar door at an independent monthly warehouse night, with a late teens to twenties crowd who follow the night rather than the venue. The band is load bearing. Push it up into restrained typography, a clean neutral grade, generous white space and a considered logo lockup and it reads as a hundred dollar festival brand or a corporate venue takeover, which is precisely the thing this audience treats as evidence that the night has been bought and is no longer theirs. Push it further down into cluttered stacked promoter text, clip art and drop shadows and it reads as a flyer nobody made, which is a different kind of dead. The correct answer is loud, immediate and slightly rough on purpose: a dark ground, saturated stage colour left in rather than corrected out, display type doing real work, and a mark that looks painted rather than drawn. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even where every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 350 to 900 dollars, and the tight turnaround is the real constraint on how much archaeology is affordable.

brand_identity.about: Pulsevault is an independent monthly club night in a Cleveland warehouse, run by a small crew and promoted almost entirely on social in the days after each event. Door is 20 to 30 dollars, the room is late teens to twenties, and the night lives or dies on what goes up before the next tickets drop. brand_identity.audience: Late teens to twenties, following the night rather than the venue. They read agency polish as proof the night has been bought and is no longer theirs.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A 20 to 30 dollar door at an independent monthly night. Positioned deliberately rough: loud and immediate, kept clear of both a 100 dollar festival brand and a homemade flyer nobody made.
brand_identity.typography: Display: a heavy, loud display cut doing real work, painted or condensed, with attitude. Text: a plain grotesque for the lineup and details, legible at story size. Loud, never corporate, never clip art. The type should feel like the room, not an advert.
brand_identity.voice: Direct and hyped but never fake, written the way the crew actually talks. Example line: 'Saturday. Warehouse. Tickets Tuesday. Do not sleep on it.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Pulsevault has never had a logo file. The mark exists only hand painted on the brick beside the entrance and survives as one photograph taken at the end of the night under a single floodlight. The wordmark has to be recovered from that photograph as artwork the night can reuse, and it has to hold on a cover that is close to black. There is no colour spec and no prior guideline. The one thing the night reprints unchanged is a plain lineup card its print shop runs a small batch of each month, supplied as last month's flat press artwork: the running order and the per act details change every date, the layout does not.
brand_identity.values: It belongs to the crowd: made by the people who run the night, not bought in.

assets_supplied.name: pulsevault_floor_stills/ (7 stills, fast lens, high ISO)
assets_supplied.kind: Stills the night's photographer shot from the floor, wide open and pushed, plus one frame from a previous night that got mixed in.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A handful from the floor and one from another night that got mixed in."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The frame with the best crowd energy is the one where the crowd's shoulders and the dark ground sit at almost the same value, so a knockout bites into the edge there and reports success, and the frames are already noisy from being pushed, so a heavy grain or halftone treatment on top closes faces into mush at the size the cover actually posts while looking strong at full size. The stray frame from the previous night was lit by a different rig and nothing in its filename says so.

assets_supplied.name: pulsevault_wall_mark.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the venue's wordmark hand painted on brick beside the entrance, shot at the end of the night under a single warm floodlight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The mark only exists painted on the wall. This is the only picture of it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is painted lettering on a photographed masonry substrate, which behaves nothing like a flat scan: a prompt naming the wall returns the brick rather than the paint, the letterforms have enclosed counters that background removal cannot punch and returns as a solid plaque, and the trace arrives with no viewBox and an opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it. The right third of the wall falls away from the floodlight into shadow where paint and brick run close in value, and the hand painted strokes are thin where the brush lifted.

assets_supplied.name: pulsevault_next_date.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The details for the next night: date, doors, lineup in running order, age policy, door price and the ticket link.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything for the next one. The lineup order matters."

assets_supplied.name: pulsevault_last_flyer.png
assets_supplied.kind: Screengrab of last month's flyer the promoter made himself on his phone, supplied as a tone reference rather than as artwork.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Roughly the energy. Do not copy it, it was made on my phone at four in the morning."

assets_supplied.name: pulsevault_lineup_card_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The flat press artwork the night's print shop runs for its monthly lineup card: one A6 card, a near black ground with a full bleed floor still behind a painted style masthead, one act's name and slot, a set time and a billing pill.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last month's card. Keep it the way it is, we only swap the names, the times and the picture."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It reads as four tidy fields over a photo, but the act name, the slot and the set time are one continuous text story in a single frame rather than three addressable fields, and the mapping readout for that frame silently omits the billing run while keeping its line break, so every offset computed past it is short by exactly that run and the validator still returns valid. The act name sits in a fixed measure that does not spill, so a value longer than last month's stops rendering at trim with no overset flag. The picture area is a real graphic frame but at a fixed tall card proportion unlike the landscape cover crop, so a frame cut for the cover cannot be reused and each act needs its own crop to the card's proportion. The media box equals the trim with no bleed box, so a press ready with bleed delivery cannot be honoured from it however the render is called.

assets_supplied.name: pulsevault_lineup.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The next date lineup as a sheet, one row per act in running order: slot, act name, set time, billing and the frame to sit behind each card.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The lineup as a sheet. The order is the order, do not move it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The set times are typed inconsistently across the rows the way the promoter typed them, one act's picture cell is simply blank because no frame was picked for it and no header reveals it, and the headliner's picture cell points at the one floor still that came from a previous night under a different rig, whose neutral filename says nothing, so a run that trusts the sheet prints another night's cool lit frame behind the most visible card. The running order is load bearing and must not be reordered, and the date itself is not in the sheet because it is fixed template text on the card.
